title: The prophet sequence
statement: Per the canon, the prophets of the world's religious traditions were operational interlocutors between the Elohim and specific peoples and eras: contacted, briefed, and tasked figures — Moses, Elijah, Jesus, Muhammad, and the founders the canon enumerates — each delivering the message in the register his era and culture could carry, which is the mechanism behind the canon's claim that the religions testify to the same creators (woh-claim-0027); the corpus records the sequence at collective level, with per-figure records minted only where the corpus develops them.

includes: The role definition: prophet as contacted interlocutor — briefed, tasked, era-adapted — rather than as inspired mediator of an immaterial divine
The sequence as the canon enumerates it, at collective level, with the era-adaptation clause carrying the traditions' differences as design rather than error
The testimony mechanism: the sequence is how woh-claim-0027's enumerated traditions come to testify to the same creators
Instance records: woh-claim-0037 (Jesus) is the sequence's first per-figure record; others are minted as the corpus develops them
excludes: Uniformity of contact mode or briefing depth across figures; the canon differentiates and so does the record
Adjudication of any tradition's own account of its founder; each is preserved in its own voice, per the comparative discipline
Figures the canon does not enumerate; the sequence is closed to canon-named members plus canon-stated criteria
The Daniel-era emissaries of woh-claim-0006, which are a different operational category (delegations to powers, not prophets to peoples)

source_references.locator: TBWTT-5:54 (the traditions enumerated as testifying); the prophet-briefing material across the narrative chapters (Moses, Elijah, the sequence's frame)
The Qur'an's own prophet-sequence theology (the messengers to every people) — the tradition-internal parallel the record engages without conflating
The academic account of the movement's prophetology

alternatives.statement: Prophet-sequence structures are internal theological developments (Islamic prophetology above all); the canon generalizes a pattern the traditions built for their own reasons.
The canon's enumeration tracks the religions a 1970s French audience would recognize; the sequence's membership is sociological, not historical.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0027 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the role definition or the enumeration.
Public prose begins minting per-figure claims without records or adjudicating traditions' self-accounts, both of which this record excludes.
